clue.text: Non-U music, rota played displaying lack of beat

indicators.note: something played is performed freely, so the letters are rearranged as in an improvisation
non-U says the letter standing for U is to be absent from what follows

parts.note: taken as written, then losing its U
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rota of players performs common music that has no rhythm to it.
explanation.walkthrough: Non-U is also the snob's label for vulgar taste, which makes the music sound lowbrow. Remove U from MUSIC, add ROTA and rearrange to get ACROTISM.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrotism is the medical term for an absent or imperceptible pulse, so the heart shows no beat.

clue.text: Tuck I cooked after church? Stop (7, two words)

indicators.note: cooking transforms ingredients, so these letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: CH is the standard abbreviation for church
the five letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether to eat after the church service, then calls a halt.
explanation.walkthrough: Tuck is British school slang for food, which is why cooking it seems natural. Here the word placement says CH comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Chuck it is an informal command meaning give up or cease what you are doing.

clue.text: It's played out in the ring? Copy in France I turned up within

definitions.text: It's played out in the ring?

indicators.note: within places one piece inside the other

parts.note: Roneo was a duplicating machine, so to roneo is to copy

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: je is French for I, then turned to read EJ

explanation.surface: A cryptic hint at a circus act, then an instruction about copying something in France.
explanation.walkthrough: The ring suggests a circus or boxing, but it is the bullring. Roneo was a trade name for a stencil duplicator, hence copy.
explanation.definitionFit: Rejoneo is bullfighting on horseback, a spectacle performed in the bullring, hence the playful question mark.

clue.text: Active worshipper absorbing potential energy

indicators.note: absorbing means taking something in, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: an orant is a praying figure in early Christian art
PE is the physics abbreviation for potential energy

explanation.surface: An energetic churchgoer soaks up the force of potential energy.
explanation.walkthrough: An orant is a figure shown praying with raised arms, common in early Christian art.
explanation.definitionFit: Operant means operating or producing effects, as in operant behaviour, so it is a formal synonym.

clue.text: What's contained in certain remarks against everyone (5, two words)

indicators.note: contained in says the letters lie inside the words that follow

parts.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Asks what some comments contain that is aimed at all people.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across certaIN REMarks.
explanation.definitionFit: In legal Latin an action in rem binds the whole world, unlike one in personam directed at a particular party.

clue.text: One maybe scribbling notes

indicators.note: scribbling is messy writing, so the following letters come out jumbled

parts.note: five letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A description of someone jotting down notes quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the definition and the wordplay: a jumble of NOTES gives STENO.
explanation.definitionFit: A steno, short for stenographer, takes rapid shorthand notes of dictation or speech.

clue.text: This could make medic run couch treatment?

indicators.note: the phrase says the following letters could be remade into another word

parts.note: eight letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Wonders whether a doctor could run a session on the psychiatrist's sofa.
explanation.definitionFit: A mind cure is healing by mental means; the couch is the psychoanalyst's, so this is a playful hint at psychotherapy.

clue.text: He avoids hoaxes — it's just luck

indicators.note: to avoid something is to keep it out, so those letters are dropped

parts.note: to josh is to tease or hoax
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone who steers clear of pranks puts it down to good fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: Take HE out of JOSHES.
explanation.definitionFit: Joss is Australian and pidgin slang for fortune, from the Chinese idol thought to bring it.

clue.text: Fungal phases? One's twice penetrated gynaeceum

indicators.note: to be penetrated is to be entered, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: an oda is a room in a harem, the women's quarters
Roman numeral one
the same Roman one again, as twice says

explanation.surface: A botanical riddle about fungi and the female organs of a flower.
explanation.walkthrough: Gynaeceum suggests a flower part, but here it is the women's apartments. One I goes after the O and another after the D.
explanation.definitionFit: Oidia are thin-walled spores of certain fungi, produced in a particular stage of the life cycle.

clue.text: Reliable in second rank

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second
olid means foul-smelling, as rank can

explanation.surface: Someone dependable holds the second place in a line.
explanation.walkthrough: Rank looks like a position in an order, but here it means stinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Something solid is sound and dependable, as in a solid friend or solid evidence.

clue.text: One often typing? Totty (not the first) steps in, excited

indicators.note: excited letters are stirred up and fall into a new order
not the first means the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written, then losing its first letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: An attractive woman walks in to great excitement.
explanation.walkthrough: Totty is British slang for attractive women. Drop its T, add STEPS IN and rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A stenotypist operates a shorthand machine, so typing is the job itself, often all day.

clue.text: Like impertinence in US big'un put about, irritating non-person? (11, two words)

indicators.note: putting something about turns it around and around, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: as means like
sass is American slang for cheek
the five letters rearranged

explanation.surface: An American takes cheek from a big fellow, who is annoying and not quite human.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark covers the joke: this killer is not a person but an insect whose bite irritates.
explanation.definitionFit: Assassin bugs are predatory insects with a painful bite, so the killer of the name is not human.

clue.text: Keeping the peace, police ration it possibly

indicators.note: possibly says the letters could form something else when rearranged

parts.note: eight letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Officers keeping order might hand out food in measured portions.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes the kind of police: those deployed against rioters.
explanation.definitionFit: Antiriot police are squads trained to control crowds and preserve public order.

clue.text: The first person in Paris to enter court? One'll clear the decks

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so one piece is placed within another

parts.note: to sue someone is to take them to court; also to court a lover
je is the French first-person pronoun

explanation.surface: A Parisian about to appear before the judges, then a sailor scrubbing the ship.
explanation.walkthrough: Court looks like a noun for a place of law, but it is the verb: to take to law.
explanation.definitionFit: Sujee or soogee is a cleaning solution used by sailors for scrubbing paintwork and decks.

clue.text: Edges, outsides trimmed, useless

indicators.note: trimming the outsides removes the first and last letters

parts.note: to edge along is to sidle

explanation.surface: Borders that have had their outer parts cut are no use.
explanation.walkthrough: Edges looks like a noun, but here it is the verb to edge: SIDLES.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle can mean pointless or of no effect, as in idle threats or idle speculation.

clue.text: Where music appears mostly to tear away with love, gliding

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter is kept

parts.note: music is written in a score, then cut short
to rend is to tear apart
O is zero, love in tennis

explanation.surface: A piece of music almost ripped apart, played sweetly and smoothly.
explanation.definitionFit: Scorrendo is an Italian musical direction for a smooth sliding passage, as in a glissando.

clue.text: Tripe as before requires involving recipe

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to entail is to require as a consequence
R is the abbreviation for recipe, from Latin take

explanation.surface: Tripe, made the usual way, needs a recipe.
explanation.walkthrough: As before flags an older sense: entrails once meant tripe, the stomach used as food.
explanation.definitionFit: Entrails are the guts of an animal, and tripe is stomach lining sold as food.

clue.text: Scoff attached to bustle, old Flemish cloth

parts.note: to scoff is to mock
ado is fuss or bustle

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at a lady's bustle made of antique Flemish fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: A bustle was a padded frame worn under a skirt, which sets up the cloth; here it means fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: Mockado was a woollen pile fabric made in Flanders and imitating velvet, popular in the sixteenth century.

clue.text: It may be insane in pudding, raw or burnt possibly

indicators.note: ingredients mixed into a pudding lose their order, so the letters are blended

parts.note: six letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A mad pudding recipe that could be served uncooked or overdone.
explanation.walkthrough: Raw and burnt look like cooking terms, but they name the two standard varieties of this pigment.
explanation.definitionFit: Sienna is an earth pigment sold as raw sienna or, when roasted to deepen it, burnt sienna.

clue.text: US fish, male beside a duct, swimming

indicators.note: swimming letters move about freely and settle in a new order

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for male
the five letters rearranged

explanation.surface: An American fish and its mate swim near a pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: Mudcat is an American name for various catfish living in muddy rivers, such as the flathead.

clue.text: Leaves spread about round start of tornado

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so one piece wraps the other
about suggests moving things around into a different arrangement

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

indicators.note: start of takes only the first letter of the next word

parts.note: its opening letter

explanation.surface: Leaves from trees are scattered by the arrival of a twister.
explanation.walkthrough: Leaves looks like foliage, but it is the verb: goes away. T sits inside rearranged SPREAD.
explanation.definitionFit: To depart is to go away, so departs means leaves, as a train leaves the station.

clue.text: Liar's misbehaving in clubhouse like an old clown

indicators.note: misbehaving letters do not keep their proper order
in places this group inside the other piece

parts.note: CH is a standard abbreviation for clubhouse
the five letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A liar behaves badly at the golf club, acting like an old-time joker.
explanation.walkthrough: Clown here is the old sense of a rustic boor; a carl was a churl.
explanation.definitionFit: Carlish is an old word for churlish or boorish, like a carl or rustic clown in the archaic sense.

clue.text: Ornamental style traced out on centre of baroque (7, two words)

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are thrown out of their original order

parts.note: the six letters rearranged

indicators.note: centre of takes only the middle letter of the next word

parts.note: its middle letter

explanation.surface: A decorative style is copied out over the heart of a baroque design.
explanation.definitionFit: Art Deco was the geometric decorative design movement of the 1920s and 1930s.

clue.text: Bread loaf, square, very small

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for square
totty is a dialect word for tiny

explanation.surface: A baker describes a square loaf that is very small.
explanation.walkthrough: A stotty is a flat round bread from north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Stotty or stottie cake is a heavy flat bread loaf traditional in Newcastle and the north-east of England.

clue.text: What often leads me round centre of garth, doleful?

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: the exclamation deary me

indicators.note: centre of takes only the middle letter of the next word

parts.note: its middle letter

explanation.surface: Someone sighs over the heart of an enclosed garden, feeling gloomy.
explanation.walkthrough: A garth is a yard or cloister garden. R goes inside DEARY after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreary means dismal and gloomy, close to doleful in its sense of sorrowful dullness.

clue.text: Gathered tress in loose sheets

indicators.note: gathered material is pulled together and folded, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: seven letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A lock of hair is gathered up among some scattered pages.
explanation.walkthrough: Loose seems to signal the anagram, but it belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Inserts are separate leaflets placed inside a magazine or newspaper, not bound with it.

clue.text: Fate coming up around end of fever

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the letters read from bottom to top
around means one piece encloses the other

parts.note: anon means soon, coming shortly

indicators.note: end of takes only the last letter of the next word

parts.note: its last letter

explanation.surface: Destiny arrives as a fever runs its course.
explanation.walkthrough: Coming up reads as one phrase, but coming gives ANON and up turns the result round.
explanation.definitionFit: In Norse myth the Norns are the three Fates; Norna is the singular form of their name.

clue.text: What slices blubber without ovaries, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a spayed animal has had its ovaries removed

explanation.surface: A whaling tool and a neutered female animal, joined by a pun.
explanation.definitionFit: A flensing spade is the sharp-edged tool whalers use to strip fat from a carcass.

clue.text: Comic tenor, a nuisance

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a light tenor in French comic opera
second meaning: a source of trouble or annoyance

explanation.walkthrough: The opera sense is named after Antoine Trial, an eighteenth-century French singer famous for comic roles.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who tests your patience is a burden, and the opera term names a voice type from a famous singer.

clue.text: Tit's damaged bit of ash — it hacks at seeds

indicators.note: damaged letters are knocked out of their proper order

parts.note: the four letters rearranged

indicators.note: bit of takes just one letter, the first, of the next word

parts.note: its opening letter

explanation.surface: A small bird harms part of an ash tree while pecking at its seeds.
explanation.definitionFit: Sitta is the genus of nuthatches, birds which wedge nuts in bark and hammer them open.

clue.text: Loose blouse, cheerful, French, low inside

indicators.note: inside places one piece within the other

parts.note: gai is French for cheerful
ribald means coarse or vulgar

explanation.surface: A happy French person wears a baggy top cut low.
explanation.walkthrough: Low seems to describe a neckline; it means vulgar.
explanation.definitionFit: A garibaldi is a loose shirt-like blouse modelled on the red shirts of Garibaldi's soldiers.

clue.text: Well-dressed Scottish bachelor, unrefined

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for bachelor
raw means crude or unrefined

explanation.surface: A smartly turned-out Scot, single and rough around the edges.
explanation.definitionFit: Braw is a Scots word meaning fine or handsome, especially finely clothed.

clue.text: What may accompany French ladies' underwear badly cut?

indicators.note: something cut has a part taken away

parts.note: frillies are frilly knickers
ill means badly, as in ill-treated

explanation.surface: Wonders what might go with a Frenchwoman's poorly trimmed lingerie.
explanation.walkthrough: French seems to qualify the ladies, but it is the first half of a phrase: French fries.
explanation.definitionFit: French fries is the American name for chips, so the second word follows the first.

clue.text: Excessive round pillar, wavy

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: undue means excessive
a lat is a Buddhist pillar in India

explanation.surface: An overdone column with a rippling outline.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, undulate describes an edge or surface with a wavy, rippling outline, as in botany.

clue.text: Earth left out of helmet-like structure

indicators.note: out of means one letter is taken from the word that follows

parts.note: a galea is a helmet-shaped part in botany or anatomy
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: The planet left outside a domed structure resembling a helmet.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaea or Gaia is the Greek goddess personifying the earth, mother of the Titans.

clue.text: Catching line wild pass, powerful? Puck is dispatched with it

indicators.note: catching means holding something inside
wild letters run out of control and land in a new order

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for line
the four letters rearranged
hot means potent or strong

explanation.surface: An ice hockey scene: a wild pass and a powerful strike that sends the puck flying.
explanation.walkthrough: Puck looks like the sprite from Shakespeare, but this is the hockey disc.
explanation.definitionFit: A slap shot is a hard hockey shot made with a big swinging stroke of the stick.
